intro: New product introduction planning requires precise coordination between marketing, procurement, and logistics teams. When these groups fail to align, your launch risks missing inventory targets or ballooning in cost.

blocks.text: The cost of poor new product introduction planning

When a launch coordination process fails, the financial impact is immediate and measurable. You might see lower sales growth or higher inventory costs as products arrive too early or too late. Research indicates that companies experiencing major disruptions report 6.92 percent lower sales growth on average. Additionally, these firms often face 10.66 percent higher growth in costs and 13.88 percent higher growth in inventories.

Beyond the raw numbers, the operational drag is intense. Planners spend 60 percent of their time implementing fixes for these issues. They dedicate 58 percent of their time to identifying root causes and 55 percent to finding potential solutions. This cycle of reactive work prevents you from focusing on strategic improvements.
Why launch coordination fails in complex supply chains

Launch coordination often breaks down because of structural issues. Many organizations rely on siloed spreadsheets that do not communicate with their ERP systems. This creates a fragmented view where the marketing team sees a launch date while the supply chain team sees a manufacturing bottleneck.

items: Disconnected systems that prevent real-time data flow.
Visibility gaps where inventory status remains hidden until it is too late.
Misaligned performance metrics between sales and supply chain teams.
Ignoring non-production lead times like customs and final-mile delivery.

blocks.text: Fixes for your launch coordination workflow

You can improve your launch outcomes without purchasing expensive new software. Start by establishing an Integrated Launch Team. This group should include representatives from marketing, procurement, and logistics. They must meet regularly at least 30 to 36 months before a major commercial launch to align on joint KPIs.

Next, focus on your data strategy. If you must use Excel or Google Sheets, ensure you have a single, master version of the file stored in a shared location like OneDrive or Google Drive. Never keep critical launch data in local, unshared files. Conduct formal launch readiness assessments 12 months out to identify dependencies and build recovery plans for known risks.

faq.question: What is the biggest challenge in new product introduction planning?
faq.answer: The biggest challenge is typically the lack of end-to-end visibility. When teams work in silos, they cannot see how a delay in one area impacts the entire launch schedule.

faq.question: How can I improve coordination on my Mac?
faq.answer: Use cloud-native tools that allow real-time collaboration. Ensure your browser is updated and use shared folders in your cloud storage to keep everyone on the same version of your planning documents.
